newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Megawati lawyers forced to postpone party.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Megawati lawyers forced to postpone party.

text.p: Lawyers for ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri on Tuesday postponed plans for an anniversary party and book launch after police refused to give a hotel permission to host the event.
Megawati's lead lawyer R.O. Tambunan said the Indonesian Democracy Defenders Team (TPDI) planned to commemorate their first anniversary and launch a book at an east Jakarta hotel on Wednesday.

TPDI is a coalition of lawyers, most of whom do not have formal links to Megawati's Indonesian Democratic Party, or PDI, created in the wake of her ouster to handle and coordinate the more than 100 cases around launched by her supporters to challenge her removal.
Tambunan said the hotel withdrew permission on Monday after police refused to authorise the event when asked to by hotel security staff.
They were also concerned after the hotel received two bomb threats in connection with the function, he added.
"With a heavy heart we have decided to postpone the holding of the TPDI's first anniversary and book launch until the atmosphere makes it possible," Tambunan told a news conference.
The lawyers, responsible for carrying out the lawsuits against party rivals and government officials, did not schedule another date.

Tambunan said TPDI had planned to launch "The Struggle to Capture the Fort of Justice", a book on one of their high-profile cases, as well as honour former Supreme Court judge Adi Andojo Soetjipto, known for his outspoken position on corruption in courts.
